paragraph_content.content: 7 July 2026
EQUITY: TECHNOLOGY

title_content.content: 2Q strong beat with impressive memory results Quick Note

paragraph_content.content: 2Q earnings surprise; pre-bonus OP of KRW110tn

Samsung Electronics (SEC) announced 2Q26 preliminary results with revenue of KRW171tn and OP of KRW89tn. This is a surprise, as it exceeds our OP forecast of KRW76tn. The company's OP is a quarterly profit scale of nearly 1.5-2 times that of competitors with similar market capitalization, and is at the highest level of quarterly profit among global tech companies. Considering that bonus provisions of c. KRW20tn for 1Q and 2Q26 were all reflected in the 2Q statement, we estimate that SEC's pre-bonus 2Q OP should have been around KRW110tn.

Memory strength continued; sluggish profitability of foundry/LSI and MX divisions This earnings surprise implies that SEC's memory division performance substantially beat our expectation, even considering memory price differentiation by suppliers is progressing, as mentioned in our June 24 report. We estimate the Foundry/LSI division recorded slightly improved pre-bonus operating losses in 2Q compared to the prior quarter, but the deficit scale should have grown larger upon inclusion of bonus provisions.

In our view, the Display division appears to have better-than-expected shipment volumes amid rising market share of leading companies such as Samsung and Apple (AAPL US, Not rated), but profitability appears to have declined due to price decline pressure. However, profit amount appears to be gradually growing based on revenue growth.
We estimate the MX division turned to losses in 2Q as memory price surges were being reflected in costs with a time lag. As its competitor Apple is likely to raise product prices by

, there is a high possibility that SEC will also raise smartphone prices further in 2H. However, profit improvement appears difficult as memory price uptrend is likely to continue in the third quarter as well.
Commodity memory price to grow ~20% q-q in 3Q; HBM profitability to catch up with that of commodity DRAM

We think that commodity DRAM/NAND prices will likely increase by 15-20% q-q in 3Q26F. Meanwhile, LTAs with customers should also gradually expand. Therefore, we expect the memory price growth pace to enter a gradual stabilization trend going forward. HBM, which has lower profitability than commodities', is likely to witness continued price uptrend, and we believe its profitability will converge toward that of commodity DRAM.
Maintain Buy and TP of KRW670,000; excessively undervalued vs. peers

Due to severe supply shortages, memory companies' mid- to long-term expansion plans are being more aggressive than previously planned, but we expect such efforts to have meaningful impact only after 2029F, and memory supply shortages appear highly likely to continue until then. We maintain our Buy rating and TP of KRW670,000. SEC is unfairly undervalued compared to competitors relative to its profit scale, in our view.

paragraph_content.content: Valuation Methodology Our 12-month TP of KRW670,000 is derived by applying a target P/B of 5.0x to 12MF BVPS of KRW133,139. The target multiple reflects enhanced business stability and visibility backed by memory long-term agreements. The benchmark index for the stock is the KOSPI 200.

Risks that may impede the achievement of the target price Downside risk includes potential US tariffs on semiconductor products, delay in data center construction due to power supply shortage, and slowdown in AI capex under a higher interest rate environment.

title_content.content: Definition of NOM Group's equity research rating system and sectors

paragraph_content.content: The rating system is a relative system, indicating expected performance against a specific benchmark identified for each individual stock, subject to limited management discretion. An analyst's target price is an assessment of the current intrinsic fair value of the stock based on an appropriate valuation methodology determined by the analyst. Valuation methodologies include, but are not limited to, discounted cash flow analysis, expected return on equity and multiple analysis. Analysts may also indicate expected absolute upside/downside relative to the stated target price, defined as (target price - current price)/current price.

A rating of 'Buy', indicates that the analyst expects the stock to outperform the Benchmark over the next 12 months. A rating of 'Neutral', indicates that the analyst expects the stock to perform in line with the Benchmark over the next 12 months. A rating of 'Reduce', indicates that the analyst expects the stock to underperform the Benchmark over the next 12 months. A rating of 'Suspended', indicates that the rating, target price and estimates have been suspended temporarily to comply with applicable regulations and/or firm policies. Securities and/or companies that are labelled as 'Not rated' or shown as 'No rating' are not in regular research coverage. Investors should not expect continuing or additional information from NOM relating to such securities and/or companies. Benchmarks are as follows: United States/Europe/Asia ex-Japan: please see valuation methodologies for explanations of relevant benchmarks for stocks, which can be accessed at: http://go.NOMnow.com/research/m/Disclosures; Global Emerging Markets (ex-Asia): MSCI Emerging Markets ex-Asia, unless otherwise stated in the valuation methodology; Japan: Russell/NOM Large Cap.

A 'Bullish' stance, indicates that the analyst expects the sector to outperform the Benchmark during the next 12 months. A 'Neutral' stance, indicates that the analyst expects the sector to perform in line with the Benchmark during the next 12 months. A 'Bearish' stance, indicates that the analyst expects the sector to underperform the Benchmark during the next 12 months. Sectors that are labelled as 'Not rated' or shown as 'N/A' are not assigned ratings. Benchmarks are as follows: United States: S&P 500; Europe: Dow Jones STOXX 600; Global Emerging Markets (ex-Asia): MSCI Emerging Markets ex-Asia. Japan/Asia ex-Japan: Sector ratings are not assigned.

A Target Price, if discussed, indicates the analyst's forecast for the share price with a 12-month time horizon, reflecting in part the analyst's estimates for the company's earnings. The achievement of any target price may be impeded by general market and macroeconomic trends, and by other risks related to the company or the market, and may not occur if the company's earnings differ from estimates.
